Subject: Re: Clarify annual invoice offsets / make-goods

Hi Sara — thanks for the note. Short answer up front: Redwood performs quarterly usage true-ups by default; any shortfall vs committed volume can be handled in one of three ways (invoice, invoice credit, or controlled roll-forward), depending on the account and what we agree in the SOW. The annual reconciliation synthesizes the quarters and will produce a final adjustment for the contract year.

Details and common practice:
- Quarterly true-up: we compare actual hosted API tokens used vs committed tokens for the quarter. If usage < commit, the standard path is to invoice the shortfall at the committed effective net price for that quarter. If usage > commit, we invoice overage at the agreed overage rate.
- Annual reconciliation: after year close we aggregate quarterly activity. If the account is consistently below commit but within a defined tolerance (we typically use a 5% first-year allowance), we can convert the shortfall into a one-time credit or a % discount applied to the next renewal invoice — this must be explicit in the amendment.
- Make-goods / invoice offsets: we can apply make-goods as an invoice credit rather than immediate billing only when pre-approved and documented (amendment or SOW language). Otherwise the default is billing the shortfall on the next month invoice following reconciliation.

Options I recommend for Acme based on our call:
1) Default approach: quarterly invoices with quarterly true-ups; annual reconciliation produces a catch-up invoice if there is a net shortfall.
2) Relationship-first approach (first year only): convert up to 5% shortfall into a credit applied to the next quarter (or an onboarding credit), capped at $25k. This is a one-time concession documented in an amendment.
3) Rolling offset: allow up to two quarters of roll-forward for minor shortfalls (<=3% each quarter) and settle at year-end. This requires approval from Finance.

I've attached a short reconciliation memo that explains invoicing flows and sample SOW language. If you want, Ben (sales) and Rishi (finance ops) are on copy to confirm the billing treatment and approve the cap/threshold.

Subject: Re: Internal: Acme ask — confirm preferred make-good language

Evelyn — suggestion below. Rishi, double-check plumbing for credits.

Suggested customer language (for amendment/SOW):
"Make-goods and True-up: Redwood will perform quarterly usage true-ups and an annual reconciliation. If aggregate annual usage is below the agreed committed volume, Redwood will, at Customer's election, either (a) invoice the shortfall at the contracted committed rate, (b) apply a one-time credit against the subsequent invoice, or (c) roll-forward the shortfall to the next billing quarter subject to a maximum two-quarter deferral. For Customers in their first contract year, Redwood may apply a goodwill credit for shortfalls up to 5% of the committed volume, capped at USD 25,000, provided such credit is documented in a signed amendment."

A few practical notes:
- We should avoid language that implies automatic credits without signature.
- Keep the goodwill credit as a first-year, one-time concession rather than a recurring term.
- Ben to own the sales approval; Rishi to approve the accounting treatment.

Attachment: acme-commit-amendment-draft.docx

-ben
